record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: What new heterostructure designs and theoretical models are needed to explain exchange bias, magnetic proximity, and charge-transfer effects in van der Waals magnetic interfaces and to realize large exchange bias at or above room temperature?

evidence.quote: Other effects such as magnetic proximity caused by the FM layer (Fe3GeTe2) on the AFM spins of the adjacent layer (e.g., CrCl3) at the FM/AFM interface and hence on the EB behavior have remained an open question.

Since Fe3GeTe2 is metallic and CrCl3 is semiconducting, there possibly exists "charge transfer" that occurs across this metal/semiconductor interface mediating the interfacial magnetism in this system, which should be investigated further.

In most cases, however, the large EB effect was observed at low temperature (below 100 K). Therefore, there is a pressing need for creating new heterostructure systems that can bring the large EB effect to room temperature.
It is also necessary to develop new theoretical models that can better interpret the EB and associated effects in such heterostructures.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic heterostructure consisting of a ferromagnetic (FM) layer (for example, a metallic itinerant ferromagnet such as Fe3GeTe2) stacked on an antiferromagnetic (AFM) layer (for example, a semiconducting layered antiferromagnet such as CrCl3). The exchange bias (EB) effect is the shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop of the FM along the magnetic-field axis after field-cooling through the Néel temperature of the AFM, arising from exchange coupling at the FM/AFM interface. Magnetic proximity refers to the induced modification of magnetic ordering in one layer due to the adjacent magnetic layer, and interfacial charge transfer refers to redistribution of electronic charge across a metal/semiconductor interface that can mediate interfacial magnetism.

Develop:

(a) Heterostructure design principles — specify combinations of two-dimensional van der Waals FM and AFM materials, stacking orders, twist angles, and possible spacer or capping layers — that yield a robust exchange bias field whose magnitude remains large at or above room temperature (T ≥ 300 K).

(b) A theoretical framework (microscopic Hamiltonian and/or continuum model) that simultaneously accounts for:
  (i) the exchange-bias shift and coercivity enhancement as functions of temperature, cooling field, and interface roughness;
  (ii) the magnetic proximity effect induced by the FM layer on the AFM spin configuration at the interface;
  (iii) the role of interfacial charge transfer across a metal/semiconductor van der Waals interface in mediating interfacial exchange interactions.

The framework should make quantitative, falsifiable predictions for the exchange-bias field, blocking temperature, and induced interfacial moments in terms of microscopic parameters (interlayer exchange constants, magnetic anisotropies, charge-transfer amplitudes, and stacking geometry).
artifact.status_search_result: This is a forward-looking research challenge in 2D van der Waals magnetism. Recent literature reports exchange bias in vdW heterostructures predominantly at low temperatures (typically below ~100–150 K), and unified microscopic theories incorporating proximity and interfacial charge transfer remain under active development. No published work establishes a general design or theoretical framework achieving robust room-temperature exchange bias in vdW FM/AFM heterostructures, so the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews open questions concerning exchange bias, magnetic proximity, and charge transfer in vdW FM/AFM heterostructures, noting EB is typically observed below 100 K and that new heterostructure systems and theoretical models are needed.
status_evidence.claim: The challenge of realizing room-temperature exchange bias in vdW magnetic heterostructures and developing models for proximity and charge-transfer effects is identified as open.
